source_name: Bihus.Info — Розслідування
why_relevant: Successor investigative newsroom to the original 'Наші гроші з Денисом Бігусом' programme; regularly reconstructs procurement schemes at state banks and state enterprises. Useful for identifying recurring intermediary suppliers in banking/payments hardware.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership — Ukraine impact & BI insights
why_relevant: International partner behind Prozorro/DREAM design and a steady publisher of interpretive analysis on Ukrainian procurement (single-bid premium ~7%, competitive-share trends 24.5%→70.3%). English-language bridge to Ukrainian watchdog methodology.

source_name: Government Transparency Institute / opentender.eu — corruption-risk indicator framework
why_relevant: Academic source of the single-bidding red-flag methodology that Ukrainian watchdogs implicitly rely on; maintains the Global Public Procurement Database and an extended opentender.eu risk-indicator framework. Gives a defensible, comparable scoring method for Ukrainian banking/payments tenders.

source_name: Transparency International Defence & Security — 'Six Red Flags' Ukraine
why_relevant: Concrete, Ukraine-specific enumeration of the most frequent procurement corruption risks — the checklist a watchdog applies when it flags a tender. Transferable to banking/payments equipment tenders even though authored for defence.

source_name: Центр протидії корупції (Anti-Corruption Action Centre, AntAC)
why_relevant: Major Ukrainian anti-corruption NGO whose activity explicitly includes monitoring of government procurement and advocacy shaping procurement law. Its campaigns often signal which buyers/contract types are about to face scrutiny.

source_name: ACREC — Міждисциплінарний науково-освітній центр протидії корупції (KSE/NaUKMA)
why_relevant: Academic anti-corruption research centre; the scholarly end of this cell, producing peer-style analysis of procurement integrity that complements the activist outputs.

source_name: Open Data Toolkit — «Як виявляти корупцію у публічних закупівлях»
why_relevant: Practical Ukrainian-language manual on detecting procurement corruption from open data — codifies the exact heuristics watchdogs apply, in local terminology. Directly reusable as a screening ruleset for banking/payments tenders.

source_name: DOZORRO community NGO directory (per-organisation monitoring profiles)
why_relevant: Per-NGO profile pages inside DOZORRO expose the network of regional civil-society monitors and what each one has flagged. The single best snowball vector for discovering smaller regional watchdogs that may cover local bank/payment-terminal procurements.

source_name: Громадський Простір — каталог організацій (TIU, StateWatch profiles)
why_relevant: Ukrainian civil-society aggregator carrying announcements and organisational profiles for procurement watchdogs. Useful redundancy channel when the NGOs' own sites are WAF-blocked, and a discovery route to lesser-known analytical centres.

source_name: RPR (Реанімаційний пакет реформ) — альтернативні звіти щодо антикорупційної політики
why_relevant: Reform-coalition publishing 'alternative reports' assessing anti-corruption and procurement policy implementation — an aggregated civil-society verdict that names systemic weaknesses shaping tender design.

source_name: Центр громадського моніторингу та досліджень (GMD Center)
why_relevant: Ukrainian civic monitoring and research centre surfaced alongside the main procurement watchdogs; candidate second-tier monitor whose output may cover regional/state-enterprise purchases. Not yet content-verified for banking relevance.

source_name: Prozorro — central public procurement portal (tender pages)
why_relevant: Every municipal/utility/state-enterprise procurement of e-ticketing validators, self-service payment kiosks, parking payment terminals and acquiring-adjacent 'financial services for accepting payments' is announced here. Example found: UA-2023-03-25-000455-a 'Фінансові послуги зі здійснення прийому платежів' and UA-2025-04-02-002506-a from KP Kyivtransparkservice.

source_name: BI Prozorro public analytics module (Transparency International Ukraine)
why_relevant: Qlik Sense analytics over the whole Prozorro dataset since 2015, refreshed daily, no registration. Lets you size the market for validators/kiosks/acquiring services by CPV, buyer and supplier without building your own aggregation.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — Payment Infrastructure Register / authorisation of payment service providers
why_relevant: Authoritative register of payment systems, payment system participants, technological operators of payment services and e-money issuers. This is the definitive actor list for non-bank PSPs, acquirers and e-money issuers in our cell — the population whose procurement and partner selections we then track.

source_name: NBU extended search of payment system participants
why_relevant: Searchable English-language view of registered payment systems and participants; gives transliterated official names needed to bridge Ukrainian and English source matching.

source_name: Asotsiatsiia YeMA (EMA — Association of Payment System Members)
why_relevant: 26-year-old interbank/payments association whose membership list spans payment systems, banks, finance companies, payment providers and MFIs — a ready-made actor map for the non-bank payments ecosystem, plus a payment-market news feed and a partner list that reveals vendor relationships.

source_name: Ukrainian Association of Fintech and Innovation Companies (UAFIC / FinTechUA)
why_relevant: Publishes fintech-sector catalogues and analytical studies; membership directory surfaces PSPs, e-money issuers and payment-tech vendors that never appear in banking-keyword searches.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com)
why_relevant: The main Ukrainian trade press for fintech, payments and e-commerce. Covers acquiring league tables, PSP partner and vendor announcements, and runs annual industry awards whose category lists are themselves a market map of acquirers and PSPs.

source_name: Mind.ua — payments and transport e-ticketing coverage
why_relevant: Business outlet that has produced cross-city comparisons of which e-ticket schemes actually operate in Ukrainian transport — a fast way to enumerate municipal schemes and their operators before going to Prozorro.

source_name: LeoCard — Lviv municipal e-ticket operator
why_relevant: Lviv's e-ticket scheme, notable for including private carriers' buses — the reference implementation other cities copy. Operator site plus its Facebook page announce hardware rollouts, acquirer/bank partners and scheme rules.

source_name: Kyiv Digital / Kyiv city services portal — transport card and E-ticket
why_relevant: Kyiv's official E-ticket service description, with the 1551 knowledge base explaining the Kyiv Digital transport card. Kyiv's scheme (operator KP GIOTs, Kyivpastrans validators, Kyiv Metro QR readers, Kyiv Smart Card) is the single largest payments-acceptance demand centre outside banks in Ukraine.

source_name: KharkivPass / Kharkiv E-ticket
why_relevant: Kharkiv's unified transport payment scheme ('Електронний квиток'), the third major municipal e-ticket demand centre. An unofficial companion site (eticket.kharkiv.ua) documents card issuance and acceptance details.

source_name: KP Kyivtransparkservice / Kyiv City parking administration
why_relevant: Kyiv parking is cashless-only via mobile apps and EasyPay terminals — i.e. a municipal enterprise that procures payment acceptance and awards it to a non-bank operator. Its Prozorro buyer profile carries automated parking payment-control system tenders and 'financial services for accepting parking payments'.

source_name: Fondy — PSP corporate site
why_relevant: One of the largest Ukrainian PSPs; its own blog/news channel is where partner and vendor selections, new acquiring partnerships and market expansions are announced first. Confidence in the exact domain is moderate — verify.
